clue.text: Paddy joining African party with English shows self-restraint

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of bad temper, so the word gives a synonym meaning a tantrum
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Someone prone to tantrums keeps calm by joining a political party and an Englishman, showing admirable restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' is a British informal word for a fit of anger, not a name here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: moderation and self-control in behaviour, especially abstinence from alcohol, is what this word names.

clue.text: Small thanks given to this writer, being dull

parts.note: ta is a short informal British way of saying thank you
the setter refers to themselves, giving the pronoun me

explanation.surface: A writer receives only a meagre thank-you, which makes the occasion feel flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something insipid, unexciting and lacking spirit can be called this, as in a tepid, uninspired party.

clue.text: From what we hear, honours for monkeys

indicators.note: the phrase signals that a word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: medals are honours awarded for service or bravery

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that some monkeys have been decorated with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkeys' is a verb here: to monkey with something is to tamper with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who monkeys about with things interferes and tinkers where they should not.

clue.text: Strange behaviour that is noticeable in The Oval?

definitions.meaning: odd, unconventional conduct of a quirky person
in geometry an ellipse has a measurable departure from a perfect circle, so any oval shape shows this property

explanation.surface: Odd conduct stands out at The Oval, a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, so the surface suggests a crowd's antics; the second sense is the mathematical measure of how far an ellipse departs from a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: oddity of conduct, and the geometrical quantity describing how elongated an elliptical curve is.

clue.text: A totally sober person longed to be with partner?

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol at all
to have ached for something is to have longed for it

explanation.surface: A teetotaller yearned to be in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone in a committed relationship is described as spoken for, not single, i.e. in a couple.

clue.text: Church faces test in relation to its singers

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, facing the next one, so church comes before the test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A church choir is put through an examination of its singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: relating to a choir or chorus, which is what a church's group of singers is.

clue.text: Self-satisfied son, one taken for a fool

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a mug is a gullible person who is easily duped

explanation.surface: A complacent son is treated as an idiot by others.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone complacently pleased with themselves and their achievements is described this way.

clue.text: Military poet of ancient Rome

definitions.meaning: relating to war and soldiers, as in law imposed by the army
the Latin epigrammatist from Spain who wrote witty short poems in the first century AD

explanation.surface: A soldierly poet from the classical world.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for things warlike, and the English name of the Roman epigrammatist Marcus Valerius Martialis.

clue.text: Good game with the French must include stout basic principle

indicators.note: the outer pieces must contain the next piece, which goes inside them

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a ball game
le is a French word for the
a stout person is round, plump in shape

explanation.surface: A sound game, played the French way, should involve something hearty as a fundamental rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' suggests the dark beer, but here it is an adjective meaning plump; 'must include' sets it inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fundamental rule laid down at the outset governing how something is conducted.

clue.text: Intervention when cold is caught — this being taken?

indicators.note: the first word traps the next piece inside it, as if catching it

parts.note: mediation is intervention in a dispute to reconcile the parties
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: When someone catches a cold, intervention is called for in the form of something to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's closing cryptic tail: what is being taken when a cold is caught is a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: drugs or remedies are what a patient takes to treat an illness such as a cold.

clue.text: Liveliness of brother crossing island

indicators.note: the brother goes across, straddling the island so it ends up inside

parts.note: bro is the informal short form of brother
I is the abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A spirited brother is crossing over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: vigour and spirited energy, especially in performance, as in playing with dash.

clue.text: Is smart phone designed for antisocial types?

indicators.note: the letters are designed afresh, i.e. rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Was the smartphone created for people who would rather avoid company?
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the letters of IS SMART PHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who dislike humankind and shun company are the ultimate antisocial individuals.

clue.text: Map reveals lake in hollow

indicators.note: the lake is placed inside the word for hollow

parts.note: a pan is a shallow natural hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A chart shows a lake lying in a depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Map' is a verb: to map out a course is to work it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as a verb, to map out or chart a course of action in advance.

clue.text: Firm came down to meet one about partnership arrangement

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
alit is a past tense of alight, to descend or land
the Roman numeral for one is I
on means about, concerning, as in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: A company's boss came down to meet someone about a joint venture deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an alliance of parties for joint action, typically a government formed by several political groups.

clue.text: Bit of bread for those who can afford caviare?

definitions.meaning: the top crust of a loaf
a jocular phrase for the aristocracy and the wealthy elite

explanation.surface: A piece of bread offered to people rich enough for luxury fish roe.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally the top surface of a loaf, and idiomatically the highest social class, the moneyed elite.

clue.text: Father's attempts to make small cakes

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive s
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at baking little cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: items of baked dough such as tarts and Danishes, small sweet baked goods.

clue.text: Bricklayer cum jazz musician?

definitions.meaning: someone who builds walls, especially dry-stone ones
Fats ... was an American jazz pianist and composer

explanation.surface: A builder who doubles as a jazz performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who builds walls, and the surname of the stride pianist Fats Waller.

clue.text: Imitation of historical rebel, leader of insurgents captured

indicators.note: the outer pieces take the next letter prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: past means belonging to history, gone by
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A copy of a famous historical rebel, with the head of the insurgents taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The rebel is Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary; 'captured' means the other pieces hold the insurgents' leading letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an artistic work that copies the style of another, a derivative pastiche being a stylistic imitation.

clue.text: Attract only some apprentices

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Only a few trainees are drawn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lure or tempt someone, drawing them in with an offer.

clue.text: What could be great as riot controller

indicators.note: the letters could be reshaped into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something great as a way of keeping a riot under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the letters of GREAT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an irritant gas used by police to disperse crowds and control rioting mobs.

clue.text: Mass dumped in waterway in a Swiss region

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: belonging to a canton, an administrative division of Switzerland

indicators.note: the mass is thrown into the waterway, ending up inside it

parts.note: a canal is an artificial waterway
a ton is a unit of mass or weight

explanation.surface: A great weight is tipped into a canal somewhere in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: relating to a canton, one of the states making up the Swiss confederation.

clue.text: When row follows end of session it's less pleasant

indicators.note: the row is placed after the preceding pieces
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tier is a row of seats, one above another

explanation.surface: When an argument breaks out at the close of a meeting, things turn unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative synonym: more unpleasant, meaner or more horrid than something else.

clue.text: Great number, say, being eaten by wild animal

indicators.note: the first piece ends up inside the animal, swallowed

parts.note: a lion is a wild animal
eg, for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: A large crowd, for instance, devoured by a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vast multitude, as in 'their fans are many', originally a Roman army unit.

clue.text: Most gossipy woman's appearing in court

indicators.note: the woman's name is placed inside the word for court

parts.note: Hattie is a woman's name, here with the possessive s

explanation.surface: The most talkative woman turns up in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: the most talkative, most fond of idle chatter and light conversation.

clue.text: When speaking, regrets trick

indicators.note: the word is to be taken as it is pronounced aloud

parts.note: rues means regrets, as in rue the day

explanation.surface: A speaker regrets a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ploy or stratagem designed to deceive someone.

clue.text: Wait on, needing time to finish

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone waits on a table and needs time to finish up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to look after or attend to someone's needs, as a nurse does for patients.

clue.text: Our gentlemen must suppress this desire

indicators.note: the words hold down, i.e. contain, the answer within them

explanation.surface: Our menfolk must restrain this craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a strong wish or impulse, an itch to do something.

clue.text: Record reversal of very good policy for establishing control

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the following word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: pi is an informal word for pious, very good
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A record U-turn on a good policy for bringing things under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very good' giving PI is a crossword convention, short for pious; 'reversal of' turns only that piece round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: orderly behaviour enforced by rules, i.e. the regulation and order kept in a school or army.

clue.text: Flipping thing that occurs at Lord's before play

definitions.text: Flipping thing that occurs at Lord's before play

parts.words: Flipping thing that occurs at Lord's before play
parts.note: before a cricket match a coin is flicked into the air to decide which side bats first; 'Flipping' also hints at a mild expletive

explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a London cricket ground; the captains spin a coin there before the start, and the call decides who bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: the spin of a coin by the captains at the start of a cricket match.

clue.text: Deem Uranus somehow to be very large?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in some other way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the planet Uranus is of enormous size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of DEEM URANUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: so vast as to be beyond measuring, immeasurable or limitless.
